figures.finding: Eswatini taxes residents and non-residents alike on Eswatini-source income: 20% to SZL 100,000, 25% to SZL 150,000, 30% to SZL 200,000 and 33% above, less a rebate of SZL 8,200 a year (SZL 10,900 over 60), so no tax falls below SZL 41,000.
figures.applies: Tax year 1 July to 30 June; PwC reviewed 30 March 2026 (year to 30 June 2026).

sources.said: 0 100,000 SZL 0 plus 20% of taxable income in excess of SZL 0 100,000 150,000 SZL 20,000 plus 25% of taxable income in excess of SZL 100,000 150,000 200,000 SZL 32,500 plus 30% of taxable income in excess of SZL 150,000 200,000 and above SZL 47,500 plus 33% of taxable income in excess of SZL 200,000
A rebate of SZL 8,200 (SZL 10,900 for those over age 60) per annum is applied to the annualized tax calculated. In essence, no tax is payable below an annual taxable salary of SZL 41,000 per annum .

figures.finding: Eswatini has no social security contributions; employed persons pay a graded (poll) tax of SZL 18 a year.

sources.said: There are no social security contributions in Eswatini. There is, however, a graded tax (poll tax) of SZL 1.50 per month for all employed persons payable in advance in full on 1 July (i.e. SZL 18.00).

figures.finding: Employees are taxed through PAYE; payments for services by contractors or professionals in Eswatini bear 15% withholding.

sources.said: Individuals in paid employment are subject to the pay-as-you-earn (PAYE) system.
Contractors or professionals WHT is payable at the rate of 15% on services provided by contractors or professionals in Eswatini

figures.finding: A public entertainer not ordinarily resident in Eswatini bears 15% withholding on income earned there, deducted by the payer and paid within 15 days; royalties bear 15%.

sources.said: Entertainers and sportsmen WHT is payable at the rate of 15% on income earned in Eswatini by entertainers and sportsmen. This tax relates only to public entertainers and sportsmen not ordinarily resident in Eswatini. The payer is required to deduct the tax and pay it within 15 days.
WHT for royalties and management fees is payable at the rate of 15%.
VAT is charged at the standard rate of 15%.

figures.finding: The tax year runs 1 July to 30 June; returns are due within 120 days of 30 June.

sources.said: The tax year runs from 1 July to 30 June.
are required to file returns within 120 days of 30 June.
